I study labor markets shaped by high informality, and what happens when social
insurance is extended to workers who sit outside a formal contract. Most of my
work uses Mexican administrative and survey microdata to evaluate policies that
are already on the books.

I am a Research Economist in the Real Sector Research Division at
[Banco de México](https://www.banxico.org.mx/). I hold a PhD in Economics from
Stanford University, where I was a
[Knight-Hennessy Scholar](https://knight-hennessy.stanford.edu/), and BA and MA
degrees from ITAM.

**Current work.** [Social Insurance Without a Job](research/working-papers/social-insurance-without-a-job/index.qmd)
asks whether giving students health coverage untied to employment pushes young
workers into informality. It does not. Read the
[explainer](files/social-insurance-without-a-job-slides.html){target="_blank"}
or see [Research](research.qmd) for the rest.

**Labor Market MX** recomputes the ENOE's headline labor indicators from
microdata every quarter, validated against INEGI's own published bulletin.
[See the data](data.qmd).
